_why: These STLs do not come back from the generator that the pack standard calls
the geometric source of truth. The drift is INHERITED: every entry is present
in this repo's first commit, the handoff exactly as delivered, so the bundle
shipped STLs exported from an earlier revision of the generator than the one
it also shipped. Nothing done in this repo introduced any of it, and the 16
parts that were regenerated here all reproduced faithfully first (largest
Nothing here has been regenerated, deliberately. Four files are ROTATED
relative to the generator and four more are MIRRORED or shifted. Print
orientation is a real decision and the STL is what a builder slices, so
regenerating would re-orient parts on a guess about which copy is correct.
Whoever owns the design decides that, and the first test print settles it.
Rebuild: node tools/reexport.js <slug> <part> && npm run clean-mesh
(only once you know the generator is the copy to trust)
then delete the entry here. Validation fails on a file that drifts and is not
listed, and on a listed file that no longer drifts, so the list cannot rot.
Tolerance is 1e-5 mm. The page centres parts in float32 while the Node path
uses doubles, so untouched parts still disagree by about 2 nanometres.
